symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: docx_text() dropped characters Word writes as Symbol-font w:sym elements, and a table cell holding nothing else was dropped with them. cth_convert_sym_v12.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0B4 ×, F0B0 ° and the like, and the brace pieces F0EF ⎪, F0FC ⎫, F0FD ⎬, F0FE ⎭), Wingdings boxes to "[ ]", and private-use code points U+F0xx the same way; run with its mapping switched off it reproduces the first deposit byte for byte.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.what_changed: The Fourth Schedule's table (period of service for pension, section 39) draws a large brace in a cell of 11 rows, built from 80 Symbol brace pieces (11 ⎫, 11 ⎬, 11 ⎭, 47 ⎪). They are layout only: each groups a row's ranks against its number of years. The first conversion dropped the pieces and so the cells; the reconversion restores them as 11 new lines (one per cell, e.g. "⎫ ⎪ ⎪ ⎬ ⎪ ⎪ ⎪ ⎭"), inserted after lines 1386, 1387, 1388, 1389, 1391, 1392, 1393, 1394, 1396, 1397 and 1398 of the first deposit. A diff shows no other change; no word or number of the text changed. Lines after 1386 move down by up to 11 (2,542 lines, was 2,531); the formulas sidecar's line references are all before line 1386 and still hold.
